en.title: Global Macro — Higher bond yields and divergent interest-rate decisions expose the limits of oil relief
en.deck: US job openings at 7.5 million, Treasury ten-year yields at 4.95%, an Australian rate hike, softer crude and Brazil's 1.42% equity decline show why lower energy futures are not yet broad financial easing.
en.regime: Resilient US vacancies and selected AI equities coexist with near-5% sovereign yields, Australian monetary tightening, cheaper oil futures and regional credit and currency stress.
en.key_risk: Mistaking lower oil futures and positive technology equity returns for confirmed disinflation or generalized credit easing.

contrary_evidence: US JOLTS vacancies remain strong but gross hiring and separations do not establish accelerated net payrolls or wage growth.
3 November Nasdaq and S&P gains diverge from the Dow loss and Brazil's Ibovespa decline; no general global equity recovery established.
Oil futures settled lower on 3 November but no signed Iran peace accord or physical normalisation of Hormuz deliveries established.
Australia's RBA tightened 6-3 while the Brazilian Copom outcome had not occurred at cutoff, preventing an assumption of synchronized easing.
Market expectations in B3 Copom options and Focus do not constitute the Central Bank's actual future decision.
Eurostat 4 November inflation flash and US election national outcomes were not established at cutoff.
limitations: Information cutoff 00:39 BRT on November 4, 2026; current 4 November releases and later US election counting omitted.
Oil figures are dated 3 November futures settlements and not verified physical cargo flows.
B3's own informational publication reports 165528.92 close, while other media sources show differing final/indicative values; source distinction must be checked during QA.
US Treasury constant maturity yields derive from indicative market quotations and not a live bond transaction for the exact constant maturity.
Labour observations refer to September while market observations refer to November 3; cross-period comparisons describe mechanisms not an estimated causal model.
English and PT-BR drafts were prepared by the same producer and require independent methodological, substantive, and bilingual editorial QA before publication.
